correctness.rationale: Each cycle edge is geodesically essential exactly in 0<w<n−1. The unit ball is the hull of exposed normalized edge molecules; dual ball is the exact weighted single-hyperplane cube slice. A vertex has at least n−1 saturated coordinates, by a two-coordinate perturbation and rank argument. McGregor’s criterion then gives the index-one property precisely when no extreme dual point has an interior coordinate; explicit patterns prove all strict failure regimes, while parity proves the sole strict-cycle success. For w≥n−1 the metric is exactly a path and free space equals real ℓ1^(n−1). Real n≥3 and every w>0, with equality boundaries, are covered without finite tests.

value.rationale: Complete sharp natural weighted-cycle classification of maximal numerical index, including all dimensions n≥3 and positive parameter w. Identifies instability of the unweighted bipartite index-one result under arbitrarily small single-edge perturbations, then recovery at the exact point of metric redundancy. Cycle is the elementary non-tree graph, so this boundary is a natural stability problem rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The precise index in strict failure regimes is not claimed.
